summary: Rotating service-account warmup heartbeats triggering tenant 429s in Dedicated VPC
description: Issue summary: Customer reports periodic waves of 429s affecting interactive traffic after enabling an automated credential rotation process for a set of background workers that perform model warmup and health-checks. Impact: ~15% of interactive requests in the tenant were rejected with 429 for 10-30s windows during rotations, degrading UX and causing client-side retry storms. Environment: Dedicated pool in a private VPC (prod-us-west) with scheduled credential rotation every 5 minutes for background warmup workers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs credential rotation on background service accounts every 5 minutes (short-lived tokens).
2) Immediately after rotation the background warmup workers reconnect and emit rapid health-check heartbeats and prefix-warmup requests (burst of 150-300 requests over 5-10s).
3) Interactive client traffic continues concurrently (web users and API calls).
4) Observe 429s on interactive routes for tenant during the same timeframe; console quota graph shows burst depletion.
logs: 2026-03-10T08:15:03.001Z rate-limiter: REJECT tenant=nebulamaps route=/chat status=429 requests=78 reason=token_exhaustion
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: Correlated customer timeline with rate-limiter burst depletion windows; warmup reconnects happen immediately after token rotation.

Hypothesis A (SRE): Short-lived service account rotation causes high fanout reconnects that are counted against the tenant's burst credits because warmup/health-check endpoints are treated as interactive routes.
Hypothesis B (Auth): Token rotation duplicates ephemeral keys briefly (old and new live concurrently) causing double counting on some proxies — low likelihood based on token traces.
Checked console: quota heatmap shows repeated small troughs aligned with rotation schedule. No global autoscaler events or pool evictions at the same timestamps.
Captured pcap from ingress-proxy and traced ~240 warmup connections within 8s after rotation. Each warmup sends a small 1-3 token request but aggregate consumes burst credits.
Cross-reference: customer used dedicated canary route that does not have an isolated burst pool; health-checks are routed to the same route weight as interactive endpoint.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Logged with customer after initial call. Collected timelines, sample keys, and permission to review warmup config.
NebulaMaps Ops (customer) 2026-03-10: Confirmed automated rotation every 5m, warmup worker pool size 12, parallel reconnects ~20 each rotation. Can reduce frequency if needed.

Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using a traffic generator against a staging dedicated pool. Confirmed burst credit exhaustion when health-checks are counted against tenant burst lane.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-11: Proposed mitigation - exclude warmup health-check path from tenant accounting and/or configure a separate low-priority burst pool for background workers.
Security (Auth) 2026-03-11: Verified token semantics — no duplicate counting from old/new token; counting is per-request as expected.
NebulaMaps Ops 2026-03-11: Applied a short-term change to stagger warmup reconnects and temporarily disabled reconnection fanout; reports immediate reduction in 429s.

Diego Martinez 2026-03-12: Opening internal follow-up INT-99821 to add a feature flag to exempt configured healthcheck routes from tenant burst accounting for Dedicated tenants. Linking PR once created.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: Customer staggered credential rotation + added jitter to warmup reconnects which stopped the 429 waves. Support recommended two long-term fixes: 1) Configure dedicated 'background' burst pool (priority=low) for warmup workers in Dedicated pools; 2) Add explicit exclusion for healthcheck/warmup endpoints from tenant burst accounting. SRE opened INT-99821 to track implementation and a PR was drafted to add route-level exclusion. No billing impact. Customer satisfied with mitigation and will monitor for 72h before closure.
postmortem_followup_actions: INT-99821: Implement route-level tenant-accounting exclusions for Dedicated VPCs (assigned to Diego Martinez).
Add console guidance: 'Dedicated customers: isolate warmup/healthcheck paths into a background burst pool' (docs task DOC-7310).
Add automated detection alert: repeated small troughs aligned to credential rotations should surface a support alert (OBS-512).
